excerpt_i18n.en: In front of Booth 5001 in the West Hall of the Las Vegas Convention Center, crowds gathered. At CES 2026, Qualcomm’s booth avoided piling up concepts. New releases across PCs, automobiles, robots, and the Internet of Things sketched a smart landscape spanning both consumer and industrial domains. The demo showcased a multimodal AI creation tool running seamlessly, from voice transcription generating copy to intelligent editing of image materials, with no lag or stuttering. Centered on "edge AI computing power," this approach reflects Qualcomm’s strategy of "making AI ubiquitous." In fact, the CES 2026 booth represents the culmination of nearly two decades of long-term investment by Qualcomm in AI R&D.

Meta's multi-billion dollar acquisition of Manus reflects its confidence in the evolution of "intelligent capability" from "brain-only" to "brain-and-hand" proficiency. IT veteran Li Guoping commented on Manus's change of ownership, noting that the "intelligent capability" refers to the composite ability of agents in cognition and execution. In his view, the SaaS industry is also undergoing its own intelligent transformation—"If SaaS continues to rely mainly on human-system (interface) interaction without embracing intelligent transformation, it will inevitably be overturned by the times." The fundamental shift in human-computer interaction models represents a disruptive change brought by the Agent wave to the SaaS industry.

This perspective stems from Li Guoping's decades of firsthand experience with transformative moments: in the software era, operating systems were the core of the digital world; in the PC internet era, portals and later search engines became the gateways to the digital world; in the mobile internet era, apps took over as the entry point; and in the cloud computing era, SaaS integrated and encapsulated all capabilities. Li Guoping, who worked at Microsoft for over a decade, currently serves as the Dean of the Digital Economy and Fintech Research Institute at Baiwang Co., Ltd., a leading domestic tax and finance SaaS provider. Over the nearly 20 years since the rise of cloud computing, he has consistently embraced and adopted new technological waves.

excerpt_i18n.es: Spirit, el alma, algo que los robots necesitan urgentemente en la actualidad. Pero durante el último año, el alma de los robots ha oscilado entre dos extremos. Por un lado, diversos videos deslumbrantes han inundado repetidamente las pantallas, y los "invernaderos" experimentales altamente estructurados han producido continuamente modelos con altas tasas de éxito, mostrando una IA tan inteligente en las demostraciones; pero por otro lado, cuando estos "estudiantes sobresalientes" entran en la realidad, a menudo fracasan. Los videos de demostración pueden editarse, los entornos de laboratorio pueden diseñarse específicamente, y la dificultad de las tareas puede personalizarse. Esto ha sumido a toda la industria en una confusión similar a "comparar peras con manzanas": cuando los escenarios, el hardware y los estándares de evaluación son diferentes, ¿qué estamos comparando realmente? ¿La tecnología, la inteligencia o la habilidad cinematográfica de cada uno?
